title: Coroutine give-up callback hands the caller a coroutine instead of a fallback value
text_original: Fixes #249 #412. Second PR after breaking down https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/433 (follows https://github.com/jd/tenacity/pull/434). After DRYing the `iter()` function, make `AsyncRetrying` support `async` callbacks.
text_rewritten: When retries are exhausted we return a degraded payload instead of raising, so we configure a give-up callback. On the asynchronous path that callback has to await a cache write, so it is a coroutine function — and what the caller ends up holding is an un-started coroutine object rather than the payload the callback was supposed to build. The callback body never runs, and Python warns that a coroutine was never awaited. An ordinary callback in the same slot returns its value correctly, so the value the callback produces clearly is what gets handed back; it just is not awaited first.

acceptance_hint: When the attempt budget is exhausted on the asynchronous path, a coroutine give-up callback runs and the value it produces is exactly what the caller receives; an ordinary callback keeps behaving the way it does today.
